Pleiotropic and linkage disequilibrium parts of G

Source: R/accessors.R
g_decomposition.Rd

Splits the G matrix of the current population into the G expected without associations between loci (genic) and the remainder (ld), due to linkage disequilibrium between loci and departures from Hardy-Weinberg. All matrices use the n - 1 denominator of stats::cov(), so G = genic + ld.

Usage

g_decomposition(pop, method = c("genic", "shuffle"), shuffles = 10)

Arguments

pop

an evomod_population.

method

"genic" or "shuffle", see above.

shuffles

number of shuffled populations averaged (method = "shuffle").

Value

A list with matrices G, genic and ld.

Details

  • method = "genic" (exact; architectures where genotypic values are sums of allele effects, additive() and binary_b()): twice the sum over loci of the covariance of allele effects, pooling both alleles of every individual.

  • method = "shuffle" (any architecture, including multilinear()): at each locus the 2n allele copies are pooled and randomly reassigned to individuals, which removes associations between loci and within loci but keeps allele frequencies and every allele's full state (its effect vector, or its y and column of B). genic is the mean G of shuffles shuffled populations (do O & Whitlock 2023 call it the pleiotropic part of G). For additive architectures its expectation is the exact genic part.

References

do O, I., & Whitlock, M. C. (2023). The evolution of genetic covariance and modularity as a result of multigenerational environmental fluctuation. Evolution Letters, 7(6), 457-466.

Examples

model <- evomod_model(additive(loci = 20, traits = 2),
                      mutation(rate = 0.01, cov = 0.1), init_sd = 0.1)
pop <- evolve(model, stabilizing(20, omega = 10), n = 100, seed = 1)
g_decomposition(pop)
#> $G
#>            trait1     trait2
#> trait1 0.47362851 0.02699102
#> trait2 0.02699102 0.40358214
#> 
#> $genic
#>             trait1      trait2
#> trait1  0.51782676 -0.02774668
#> trait2 -0.02774668  0.44735322
#> 
#> $ld
#>             trait1      trait2
#> trait1 -0.04419825  0.05473770
#> trait2  0.05473770 -0.04377108
#> 
g_decomposition(pop, method = "shuffle", shuffles = 20)
#> $G
#>            trait1     trait2
#> trait1 0.47362851 0.02699102
#> trait2 0.02699102 0.40358214
#> 
#> $genic
#>              trait1       trait2
#> trait1  0.530295375 -0.007434872
#> trait2 -0.007434872  0.452740317
#> 
#> $ld
#>             trait1      trait2
#> trait1 -0.05666687  0.03442589
#> trait2  0.03442589 -0.04915818
#>
